title: Jonah and the Vow
premise: Kestrel Montrose has spent a decade hiding behind her pen name, Sable Coldharbour, writing romance novels while keeping the Cornish lighthouse her grandfather left her. When a snowstorm traps her with Jonah Vane—the man she loved at twenty-two and abandoned to save her family's home—and his business rival Marcus Hale, who is secretly negotiating to buy the lighthouse out from under her, all three secrets surface in one impossible week. Kestrel must choose between selling the lighthouse to fund her sister's medical debt or fighting for it with Jonah's help, and between the anonymity that protects her and a love that demands she be seen. In the end she publishes under her own name, signs the deed over to a heritage trust with Jonah as co-trustee, and admits that second chances arrive exactly on time for those brave enough to keep the light burning.
about_author: Sable Coldharbour writes love stories from a converted signal station on the Cornish coast, where she keeps an actual lamp lit during winter storms. She insists every novel begins with a real mistake she refuses to confirm.

chapters.title: The Lamp Room
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She maintains the lighthouse alone through a failing autumn season, drafting her next novel and dodging her agent's calls about a film deal. Establishes her invisibility as armor and the debt threatening her sister Nell. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Deadline Weather
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A forecast warns of a historic snowstorm; her editor demands final revisions by Friday. Nell calls with news that treatment costs have doubled. Kestrel agrees to meet a mysterious buyer's representative before the roads close. Beat: pressure mounting from every direction.

chapters.title: The Man at the Door
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah Vane arrives soaked and stranded, sent by the buyer he now realizes is his own rival firm's client. Seeing Kestrel after ten years detonates everything he buried. He says nothing about why he came. Beat: shock masked as courtesy.

chapters.title: Two Rivals, One Roof
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Marcus Hale's car slides into the ditch; she hauls him inside too. The two men recognize each other instantly—competitors for the same acquisition—and perform civility badly. Kestrel realizes both are here for her lighthouse. Beat: claustrophobic tension with dark humor.

chapters.title: What We Were at Twenty-Two
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over candlelight and generator hum, old history leaks out: Jonah and Kestrel's summer romance, the night she vanished without explanation. Jonah's bitterness sharpens; Marcus watches, cataloguing leverage. Beat: grief resurfacing as anger.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Hunting for the deed, Marcus finds Kestrel's unpublished manuscript and deduces she is Sable Coldharbour—the author whose books he's optioned twice. He pockets this knowledge like a loaded gun. Beat: the reader learns what Kestrel most fears.

chapters.title: Snowed Under
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Roads close completely; phone signal dies. Forced proximity strips pretense—Jonah fixes the generator, Marcus flirts strategically, Kestrel cooks for enemies. A power cut leaves her and Jonah alone in the dark stairwell. Beat: warmth she can't afford.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In the blackout, Kestrel finally explains: her grandfather's will required residency, her mother was ill, and leaving Jonah was the price of survival. His fury cracks into understanding—but not forgiveness. Beat: truth offered, trust not yet restored.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus makes his pitch: a generous sum for the lighthouse, enough to erase Nell's debt entirely. Privately he hints he knows who Kestrel really is, letting the threat hang unspoken. Beat: temptation dressed as rescue.

chapters.title: Draft by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Unable to sleep, Kestrel reads her own manuscript aloud to fill a sleepless night, and Jonah realizes the heroine's lost fisherman is him—that she never stopped writing their story. Beat: devastating tenderness; the past made text.

chapters.title: Nell on the Line
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Signal flickers back just long enough for Nell to call, feverish and frightened. Kestrel nearly signs Marcus's papers on the spot. Jonah stops her hand—not with words, but by showing her the structural survey proving the buyer plans demolition. Beat: betrayal revealed.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah admits he came to buy the lighthouse himself—for a hotel chain—before his conscience mutinied. He proposes they work together against Marcus. Kestrel must decide whether a man who arrived to take her home can help her keep it. Beat: uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Storm's Worst Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm peaks; a fishing boat runs aground below the cliff. All three work the winch and lamp through the night to guide a rescue. Marcus, exhausted, shows unexpected decency. Beat: shared purpose dissolving rivalry into something human.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Dawn reveals the rescued crew safe but the boathouse destroyed. Insurance won't cover it; the lighthouse's future narrows to two doors: Marcus's money or a fight no one expects them to win. Beat: exhaustion and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: Blackmail, Gently Done
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Cornered by his own conscience and his firm's deadline, Marcus finally names his leverage aloud: sign, or he tells the world Sable Coldharbour is a lighthouse keeper playing novelist. Kestrel goes very still—and then laughs. Beat: fear transmuting into defiance.

chapters.title: The Pen Name Falls
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Instead of capitulating, Kestrel publishes an essay under her own name: 'The Woman Who Keeps the Light,' claiming her identity, her books, and her grandfather's legacy publicly. It ignites overnight. Beat: the book's turning point—visibility chosen.

chapters.title: What the World Does With You
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Fame arrives like weather: journalists at the gate, the film deal revived, fans pilgrimaging to the cliff. Jonah watches the woman he loves become public property and fears losing her to a life bigger than him. Beat: love tested by success, not scandal.

chapters.title: The Deed and the Doubt
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. With public support swelling, a heritage trust offers to protect the lighthouse—if a private co-trustee matches funds. Kestrel asks Jonah, terrified of mixing love and ledgers again. He hesitates, wounded by her assumption he'd need asking twice. Beat: misstep before repair.

chapters.title: Low Tide Confessions
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the exposed sands below the tower, they say the things ten years deferred: why he never searched for her, why she never wrote to him, what each believed the silence meant. Forgiveness arrives not as absolution but as choice. Beat: the emotional climax of the romance.

chapters.title: Marcus's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Marcus returns—not to buy, but to resign from the acquisition and hand Kestrel his firm's internal file proving the demolition plan, ending his career as he knew it. He asks only to finish the manuscript he read. Beat: antagonist redeemed at cost.

chapters.title: Signing Day
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the lamp room, Kestrel signs the trust deed with Jonah as co-trustee, Nell's treatment funded by the film deal signed under her real name. The lighthouse belongs to the future without belonging to no one. Beat: resolution of every thread—identity, inheritance, survival.

chapters.title: First Light
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, epilogue. One year later: her new novel, 'Jonah and the Vow,' publishes with her name on the cover. Jonah lights the lamp beside her as the first review copies arrive. Second chances, she writes, are for people willing to be seen. Beat: earned peace, light still burning.
